name: LUPEX (Lunar Polar Exploration)
short_status: In development, not launched: India's government cleared its share on March 10, 2025 and the two agencies signed the implementing arrangement on August 29, 2025; joint design work is underway (fifth technical interface meeting, December 2025) with launch targeted no earlier than 2028, which JAXA's Japanese page gives as Japanese fiscal year 2028, April 2028 to March 2029 (as of Oct 2026). No landing site fixed yet.

facts.label: Status (as of Oct 2026)
facts.value: In joint design and development; not launched. India's government cleared its part on 10 March 2025; implementing arrangement signed 29 August 2025; fifth technical interface meeting held in Japan 15 to 17 December 2025; an ISRO delegation visited Tanegashima in April 2026

facts.label: Who builds what
facts.value: JAXA provides the H3 launch vehicle and the rover (built by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries) plus instruments; ISRO provides the lander and several rover instruments. This inverts Chandrayaan-3, where ISRO built both lander and rover

facts.label: Mission goal
facts.value: Land near the lunar south pole and determine the quantity and quality of water ice, including in permanently shadowed regions, using a rover that drills to about 1.5 m and analyzes samples in place

facts.label: Launch vehicle
facts.value: Japan's H3-24L (the configuration JAXA calls its standard H3, with the long fairing), from Tanegashima Space Center; the H3-24L variant was confirmed at the third technical interface meeting in May 2025

facts.label: Rover
facts.value: About 350 kg including instruments, roughly 2.0 x 1.8 x 3.3 m, able to climb 25-degree slopes; built by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. It carries a 1.5 m earth-auger drill and, after a redesign that found it overweight, drops radioisotope heater units for a passive insulating scheme to survive the lunar night

facts.label: Lander and new engine
facts.value: ISRO develops the lander (about 6,000 kg), which will use a new L9 3.1 kN liquid-fuel engine from the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre; a prototype L9 was hot-fired in 2025 per ISRO's 2025-26 annual report

facts.label: International payload
facts.value: The rover carries Japanese instruments (LTGA, TRITON, ADORE, ALIS), Indian instruments (ISAP, PRATHIMA, WaSSPeR, MIR), a NASA neutron spectrometer (subsurface hydrogen to about 1 m), and ESA's EMS-L mass spectrometer, originally built for Russia's Luna-27 and redirected after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine

facts.label: India's approval
facts.value: India's government cleared its participation on 10 March 2025 (some accounts say March 13 or 14), the gating step; Japan had funded and greenlit its side years earlier

facts.label: Implementing arrangement
facts.value: ISRO and JAXA signed the LUPEX/Chandrayaan-5 implementing arrangement during Prime Minister Modi's Tokyo visit on 29 August 2025, formalizing the partnership

facts.label: Operating lifetime
facts.value: Designed to operate at least about 3.5 months on the surface, up to a maximum of about one year; the mission concept is planned to last well over 100 days

facts.label: Target launch
facts.value: No earlier than 2028: JAXA's English project page says no earlier than 2028 and its Japanese page gives Japanese fiscal year 2028 (April 2028 to March 2029), while some Indian summaries say 2027-2028 (as of Oct 2026). No firm date is manifested

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: No public total-cost figure has been released for LUPEX, unlike the Rs 2,104 crore Chandrayaan-4 approval; India's share was cleared without a published budget line

facts.label: Landing site
facts.value: Not fixed as of October 2026: candidate sites in the south polar region, near permanently shadowed regions, were still under discussion at the December 2025 technical interface meeting

timeline: JAXA and ISRO begin joint study of a polar rover mission, then widely referred to as Chandrayaan-4; Japan proceeds toward funding while India's approval stays pending for years
India's government clears its participation in LUPEX/Chandrayaan-5, the long-pending gating step (some accounts date it March 13 or 14)
Third technical interface meeting in India; the H3-24L is confirmed as the launch vehicle and landing-site options are deliberated
ISRO and JAXA sign the LUPEX/Chandrayaan-5 implementing arrangement during PM Modi's Tokyo visit
ISRO hot-fires a prototype of the lander's new L9 3.1 kN liquid-fuel engine, per its 2025-26 annual report
Fifth technical interface meeting held in Japan: development progress reviews, H3 interface coordination with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, and lander-rover interface adjustments
An ISRO delegation visits Tanegashima Space Center to prepare development activity
Launch on H3-24L from Tanegashima; JAXA gives no earlier than 2028 on its English project page and Japanese fiscal year 2028 on its Japanese page (as of Oct 2026)
